title: validate_article_ingress re-validates GroupName objects that are already validated
description:
crates/core/src/validation.rs validate_article_ingress() step 4 (lines ~165-169) calls GroupName::new(group.as_str()) on each element of h.newsgroups, which is already Vec<GroupName>. The GroupName newtype only exists to prevent invalid names from being constructed; calling GroupName::new on an already-constructed GroupName is a no-op identity check.

The comment acknowledges this: 'defence-in-depth: validate the raw string even though GroupName::new() should have already rejected invalid names at construction time; this catches any values injected via unchecked constructors, deserialization paths, or future API changes.'

The unchecked constructor GroupName::new_unchecked exists only under #[cfg(any(test, fuzzing))]. Deserialization via serde could bypass the check — that is the real risk. The fix is to implement a custom Deserialize for GroupName that calls GroupName::new and rejects invalid names, then remove the defence-in-depth re-validation loop in validate_article_ingress. This way the type itself guarantees its invariant through all construction paths, and the comment and loop become unnecessary.
